_format: Each line is one Chatterbox take. Tokens split on spaces. [shown=spoken] gives a spoken form (underscores = spaces). Suffix *y = yellow keyword, *r = red keyword, *g = green (safe). A trailing / ends a caption phrase. fx: volunteer = the shelter volunteer (narrator pitched up, clean); whisper = 'Hey, buddy' at your ear (thin, close, breathy); pepper = the narrator reveal (dry, very close, a hair lower). pause = silence after the line (s).
title: KEEP PRETENDING

lines.text: You got up for water at [3:12=three_twelve],/ and your cat*y was standing in the kitchen./
Not sitting.*y/ Standing.*r/
Up on his back legs,/ straight as a person/ waiting for something./
He was looking at the fridge.*y/
Then he turned his head,/ and looked at you.*r/
And you did what everyone does./
You said, "Hey, buddy."*y/ You got your water,/ and you went back to bed./
You were very good at pretending.*r/
Everyone is,/ at first./
Two weeks earlier.*y/
The animal shelter*y is loud./ Every cat is crying,/ pacing,/ pressed against the bars./
Except one./
A grey tuxedo*y with white socks,/ sitting perfectly still,/ watching you./
The card on his cage says Pepper.*y/
And under it:/ returned three times.*r/ No reason given.*r/
The volunteer laughs./
"He's perfect.*g/ People just bring him back."/
You take him home that night./
And for a week,/ he's the best cat you've ever had./
Scientists say*y cats don't see you as a person./
They see a big,/ clumsy cat.*y/
Pepper sleeps on your feet.*g/ He headbutts your hand.*g/ He purrs when you come home./
You smell like outside,/ and like other people.*r/
But there are little things./
He never makes a sound*y/ when he jumps down./
His bowl is always empty,*y/ but you never see him eat./
And when you turn around,/ he's already facing you.*r/
So you buy a pet camera.*y/ Just to watch him/ while you're at work./
On the first morning,/ the app has one clip for you./
Motion.*r/ [3:12=three_twelve]*r [AM=A_M].*r/
The video is green and grainy./ Night vision.*y/
[3:12.=Three_twelve.]/ Pepper walks into the kitchen/ on four legs./
[3:13.=Three_thirteen.]/ He sits./
[3:14.=Three_fourteen.]/ He stands up.*r/
Not like a cat reaching for something./ Like a person getting out of a chair.*r/
And he walks out of the frame/ on two legs.*r/
You scrub forward./
From [3:20=three_twenty]/ until [4:05,=four_oh_five,]/ he stands outside your bedroom door.*y/
Forty-five minutes.*r/ Not moving./ Not even his tail./
At [4:06,=four_oh_six,]/ he turns around,/ and looks right into the camera.*r/
That night you don't sleep./
And in the morning,/ Pepper headbutts your hand,/ purrs,/ and asks for breakfast,/ like always.*g/
Then your phone buzzes./
Camera moved.*r/ [4:07=Four_oh_seven] [AM.=A_M.]/
You open the app./ It's pointing at your bed.*r/
You call the shelter,/ and ask about the people who brought him back./
Two of the numbers are disconnected.*r/
The third one doesn't answer.*y/ But an hour later,/ it texts you./
It's Dana.*y/ She had him for two months./
She says she can't talk.*r/ He might hear./
Then the messages come,/ one at a time./
Did he stand up yet?*r/
Don't react.*r/ Whatever he's doing,/ he's a cat.*y/ Talk to him like a cat./
Don't change anything.*r/ Same food.*y/ Same time.*y/ Same lights.*y/ He notices.*r/
Never watch the camera*r/ where he can see you watching./
If he's in your spot on the bed,/ sleep somewhere else.*r/ Say nothing./
And don't bring him back.*r/
When I brought him back,/ I.../
That's it./ That's the last message./
You look up from your phone./
Pepper is on the counter,*y/ right behind you,/ looking at the screen.*r/
You lock it./
He blinks,/ slowly,/ and goes back to sleep./
So you follow the rules.*g/
Same food.*g/ Same lights.*g/ "Good boy."/
And it works./ For three nights,/ he's just a cat./
On the fourth night,/ you wake up cold.*y/
Pepper isn't on your feet./
He's on your pillow.*r/ In your spot.*r/
On his back,/ one arm*r across his face./
The way you sleep.*r/
Rule four.*y/ You get up without a word,/ and take the sofa.*y/
From the sofa,/ you can see the camera's little light./
Rule three says don't check it.*r/
You check it.*r/
Under the blanket,/ brightness all the way down./
On the screen,/ your bed.*y/
Under the duvet,/ there's a shape in your spot./
Not a cat-sized lump.*y/
A person.*r/
Then the picture moves./
The camera is turning,/ slowly,/ away from the bed,/ and toward the sofa./
Toward the blanket./ Toward the little glow*r/ of your phone underneath it./
The bedroom door creaks.*r/
Footsteps.*r/ Soft ones./
Two of them./ Not four.*r/
They stop beside the sofa./
Something is breathing next to you./ Slow and even,/ the way people breathe/ when they're pretending to sleep.*r/
Then four soft paws*g/ land on the cushion,/ and a cat lies down on your feet,/ and purrs./
He's decided/ to keep pretending, too.*r/
In the morning,/ everything is normal./
Except your mug*y is on the table,/ in front of your chair./
And it's still warm.*r/
There are new clips./
But he isn't standing at doors anymore.*y/
He's practising.*r/
[3:12.=Three_twelve.]/ The bathroom.*y/ He's standing on the sink,/ facing the mirror.*y/
He straightens up./ Again./ And again./
Every time,/ a little taller.*r/
[3:31.=Three_thirty-one.]/ The kitchen.*y/ He's sitting in your chair,/ at your mug,/ with his head tilted/ the way you tilt yours/ when you scroll.*r/
[3:50.=Three_fifty.]/ Your old phone on the counter/ is playing your voice memos*y out loud./
His mouth*r is moving with them./ No sound comes out./
Until the last one.*r/
That afternoon,/ the shelter emails you./ The drop-off photos*y you asked for./
Three people,/ three different years,/ each handing a carrier over the counter./
Each one smiling at the camera./
The same smile.*r/
The same little tilt of the head.*r/
And not one of them/ looks like the person on the adoption form.*r/
Cats bring their owners gifts.*y/ The things they've caught./
Every morning now,/ there's one on your pillow./ In the spot./
Day one:/ a hair tie.*y/
Day two:/ a house key,*y/ on a tag that says/ [D,=D_,]*r [2B.=two_B.]*r/
Day three:/ a hospital wristband.*y/ Marcus O.*r/ One of the disconnected numbers./
Day four:/ a phone.*r/
Cracked.*y/ Unlocked.*y/ Two percent battery.*r/
It's Dana's phone.*r/
And on the screen,/ is your conversation.*y/ From her side./
Every rule you were sent,/ was sent from this phone./
All of them at [3:12.=three_twelve.]*r/ While Pepper was asleep/ on your feet./
The glass is covered in tiny,/ round smudges.*r/
You read the rules again./
Don't react.*y/ Don't fight back.*r/
Change nothing.*y/ Don't lock the doors.*r/
Never watch the camera.*y/ Don't see it coming.*r/
Sleep somewhere else.*y/ Give him your bed.*r/
Don't bring him back.*y/ Don't leave.*r/
The rules were never there/ to keep you safe./
They were there/ to keep you still.*r/
The phone dies in your hand./
And in the bedroom,/ the camera's motor*r whirs./
You don't pack./
You wait for the middle of the night,/ because that's when he stands up,/ and you want him in the kitchen/ while you're at the door.*y/
[3:11.=Three_eleven.]*r/
You walk past the kitchen./
Pepper is on the counter,/ on all four legs,/ purring.*g/
A perfect cat./
You say, "Hey, buddy."/ He blinks./
The front door.*y/ The chain.*y/ The deadbolt.*y/
You reach for your keys.*y/
The hook is empty.*r/
Your phone buzzes./ Motion.*r/ Living room.*r/
The live feed./ It's you,/ at the door,/ from behind./
And right behind you,/ close enough to touch,/ something is standing.*r/
Taller than a cat can stand.*r/
Its head tilted/ the way you tilt yours.*r/
You turn around./
Nothing.*y/ The hallway is empty./
Pepper is on the counter,/ on four legs,/ purring./
You look back at the phone./
It's still there.*r/
Closer.*r/
And right next to your ear,/ in your own voice,/ something whispers./
"Hey, buddy."*r/
The shelter is loud./ Every cat is crying./
A carrier on the counter.*y/
"Pepper? Again?*y/ He's perfect.*g/ What happened?"/
The person handing him over/ is smiling.*r/
The same smile.*r/ The same tilt of the head./
It's you.*r/
"Nothing happened,"/ you say./
"I just think/ someone else/ should have a turn."*r/
The volunteer writes on his card./ Returned four times.*r/ No reason given.*r/
And inside the carrier,/ for the first time,/ the cat is crying.*r/
Pressed against the bars./ Over and over./ Like it's trying to say something.*r/
"Huh.*y/ He's never made a sound before."/
You walk out into the sun,/ a little too straight.*r/
You never wondered/ why I sound like you.*r/
Is your cat facing you/ right now?*r/
